question: How sensitive is the reconstructed butterfly resource geography to adding all uniquely accepted WCVP plant associations present in BCE/Clarke evidence-1-to-3 derivative but absent from frozen HOSTS for the exact matching European focal butterflies?

sources.bce: All 92 exact matched butterfly species, 83 species-level source pages, GitHub source audit run 37777242991
sources.baseline: Exact original native and contemporary plant distributions and 239-species frozen figure source

inclusion: For each source-verified butterfly, add ALL uniquely resolved accepted WCVP plant IDs labeled ABSENT from its frozen HOSTS species pairs; do not add ambiguous/unmatched IDs; no hand-picked host subset; no overwriting other 239 butterfly host sets.
analysis: Validate every one of original 239 species native and contemporary unions against frozen 239-species metrics, before modifying any host relationships; if any mismatch, stop rather than silently replacing the baseline.

Build native and contemporary WCVP botanical ranges for all additional unique accepted plant taxa using pinned source, extinction=0, location_doubtful=0, introduced=0 for native, all for contemporary.

Compute per-butterfly original and augmented accepted host count, native regions, contemporary regions, contemporary-minus-native introduced-added regions, fractions added, and exact region codes newly covered/reclassified.
Produce (a) 83-BCE-observed-subset summaries (b) 239-panel partial-augmentation descriptive sensitivity; always label all unmodified other species and source coverage.
Do not recompute fixed-margin null p-values, choose a favorable geographical subset, change manuscript data or publish the partial-augmentation numbers as a corrected global estimate.
Report whether added native hosts reclassify existing introduced-added cells as native, and whether adding host names does not change regional area.
critical_limits: BCE derived from Clarke 2024 and host records may share original cited literature with HOSTS; no independent causal replication.
Source filters evidence 1-3 include field oviposition and eggs but not necessarily adult eclosion; historical host reports need not generalize globally.
A butterfly-host relationship documented in European sources may not apply to each WGSRPD3 native or introduced region where the plant occurs.
Only European exact-binomial butterfly subset can be amended; 239-panel sensitivity is partial and nonrepresentative by geographic source.
The upper-bound envelope is structurally possible geography under additional linked botanical taxa, not predicted butterfly colonization or actual field feeding.
Original 239-species figures and GEB paper remain unchanged pending stronger causal and source provenance evidence.
